rows.question: Find the employee ID of engineers who resolved issues with the AI Model & Search Algorithm in SearchFlow that were causing decreased search accuracy and disrupting workflow?
rows.final_text:
The bug 'Inaccurate Search Results Due to AI Model Drift' in SearchFlow is tied to customer CUST-0018. eid_f4f58faa raised it in the bug-davidgarcia-SearchFlow channel. They said the AI model was surfacing less relevant messages over time, which affected the AI Model & Search Algorithm and was frustrating CUST-0018. They asked eid_4812cbd8 to take a look.

The fix was GitHub PR #55, 'Fix Model Drift in AI-Enhanced Search Results' (https://github.com/salesforce/SearchFlow/pull/55). eid_4812cbd8 wrote it, eid_f4f58faa approved it, and it is now closed. According to the PR, the model had degraded because user behaviour and data patterns changed in ways the training data did not reflect. The PR made three changes:
- It retrained the model on new data that reflects recent user behaviour.
- It added monitoring that detects drift early and starts retraining automatically.
- It improved the evaluation metrics.

Testing covered A/B comparisons against the old model, user feedback and quantitative relevance metrics, and regression checks. eid_4812cbd8 then announced in the same channel that the bug was resolved and linked PR #55.

The other results are about different bugs:
- **'Overfitting to Frequent Queries'** was reported by customer CUST-0055 and assigned to eid_de315467.
- **'Suboptimal AI Model Integration'** was fixed in PR #59. Its root cause was AI model data transformations that weren't integrated efficiently with database operations, which delayed search results.

rows.question: What is the employee ID of engineers who resolved the issue with the User Interface in SearchFlow that was causing user frustration due to the inability to interact with the application while waiting for search results?
rows.final_text:

The retrieved evidence describes one specific SearchFlow bug: "UI Freezes During Search Query Execution." In the bug-emmajones-SearchFlow channel, eid_4afd9484 reported that the UI stops responding during complex searches. The bug affects the User Interface component and impacts customer CUST-0018. That customer's contact is Paul Garcia, a Solutions Architect at FusionTech. eid_4afd9484 asked eid_21de287d to take care of the issue.

The other retrieved items are generic openers from several bug channels (bug-ianmiller-, bug-davidwilliams- and bug-georgebrown-SearchFlow). Each says that several customers are reporting SearchFlow issues that need attention. None of them names a specific bug, customer, owner or fix. The evidence also doesn't say whether the UI-freeze bug was fixed or when.

rows.question: Find the employee ID of engineers who resolved issues with the Search API in SearchFlow that were posing a significant security risk and potentially leading to data breaches?
rows.final_text:
The retrieved question wasn't included, so this answer covers what the evidence shows: the security issues reported against the SearchFlow Search API and the customer each one affected.

Security bugs in the Search API, by customer:
- CUST-0049: 'Exposed API Keys in SearchFlow Configuration'. API keys were exposed in client-side code, called a major security risk. Assigned to eid_8175da95 (channel bug-emmajones-SearchFlow).
- CUST-0089: 'Security Vulnerability in Search API'. It allowed unauthorized access to sensitive user data. Assigned to eid_d67508f1 (channel bug-emmajones-SearchFlow).
- CUST-0018: 'Improper Input Sanitization in Search Queries'. User input wasn't sanitized properly, which could allow SQL injection. Called a major security risk and assigned to eid_e01a396c (channel bug-georgebrown-SearchFlow).
- CUST-0107: 'Insecure Data Transmission in Search API'. Data was sent over an unencrypted channel. Reported by this customer and assigned to eid_a4fa6150 (channel bug-georgebrown-SearchFlow).
- CUST-0079: 'Unauthorized Access via Token Reuse'. Session tokens could be reused indefinitely, which could lead to data breaches. Assigned to eid_de315467 (channel bug-georgebrown-SearchFlow).

One more issue has no customer named: in channel bug-davidwilliams-SearchFlow, eid_b98a194c said the root cause was that the SearchFlow API didn't sanitize output data before the client application rendered it, which left it open to XSS (cross-site scripting).

Several retrieved passages were exact duplicates. They were counted once.

rows.question: Find the employee ID of engineers who resolved issues with the Database Management in SearchFlow that were causing slow search performance and impacting user productivity?
rows.final_text:
The customer affected by SearchFlow's 'Inefficient Query Optimization' bug was CUST-0115. In the bug-georgebrown-SearchFlow channel, eid_3bcf2a20 described the issue as search queries using too many resources and taking too long to run. They said it affected Database Management and impacted CUST-0115, and they asked eid_de315467 to take it [20260908-3-bb0b8]. eid_de315467 then said they would study another team's approach to optimizing execution plans to improve database management for CUST-0115 [20260911-4-fe4f9]. Later, eid_de315467 reported that the bug was resolved, with the approved PR at https://github.com/salesforce/SearchFlow/pull/51 [20260916-0-cd75c].

A separate bug-ianmiller-SearchFlow thread gives a root cause of 'inefficient query handling and lack of optimization for large datasets in our backend search engine' [20260930-1-95807]. Nothing in that message ties it to CUST-0115 or to the bug above. Another message in the same channel blames slow search responses on data fragmentation from frequent updates and deletions, which increased I/O operations [20261102-1-eaa35]. That appears to be a different issue.
